title: I wired frontier models into my pickleball game and made them face off
author: SanguineSpring
selftext:
There's been some discussion here recently about having models play your own game for testing so I figured this could be interesting to people. 

My goal was to have the models play in as unadulterated a state as possible—mostly image data rather than dumping full JSON state every tick. To stay within token limits, I queried each model at 2 key points per exchange (right after the opponent's contact and right after its own contact), keeping each rally in one conversation.

Raw frames alone led to silly misses, so I added the minimum needed to play off still images: ball/player velocities, drag & friction for bounce estimation, and literal pixel guidelines on the court.

The real unlock was adding a reflection loop to fix cross-rally amnesia: each model logs a short reason with each action, then reflects after the rally to write 3 takeaways carried into the next rally's prompt. That cut way down on harness tinkering and is where realistic, distinct playstyles really showed up.
